Secondary_Symptoms: Rapid increase in size of the mass
No pain associated with the mass

patient_actor_hidden.Past_Medical_History: No significant past medical or surgical history. No family history of breast cancer.

objective_for_doctor: Evaluate and diagnose the patient presenting with a breast mass.

turns.doctor_opening: Hello, what brings you in today? Could you tell me about yourself and what's been going on?
turns.patient_opening: “About four weeks ago I noticed a mass in my left breast, and it’s been rapidly getting bigger. I don’t have any pain with it, and I haven’t noticed any skin or nipple changes, and I’ve had no recent trauma or infections.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any swelling in your joints?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any swelling in my joints or any other joint-related symptoms.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any bumps, sores, or unusual growths on your scalp?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any bumps, sores, or unusual growths on my scalp. I’ve mainly just been concerned about the rapidly enlarging mass in my left breast.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been experiencing any itching or discomfort in your skin lately?
turns.patient_answer: “Not really—no itching or unusual discomfort in the skin. The main thing I’ve noticed is that the left breast mass has been getting larger quickly over the past four weeks.”

turns.doctor_question: Do you have any trouble lifting your arms above your head?
turns.patient_answer: “Yes, I don’t think I have any trouble lifting my arms above my head, and I’m not noticing any particular limitation or weakness. The main issue has been the rapidly enlarging mass in my left breast over the last four weeks.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any loss of vision that isn’t accompanied by pain?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t had any loss of vision, and it hasn’t been accompanied by pain either. My main concern remains the rapidly enlarging mass in my left breast over the past four weeks.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you had a fever that’s been so high it feels like you’re burning up—something above 104°F (40°C) that makes you feel extremely hot or dizzy?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t had any high fever or felt extremely hot, dizzy, or burning up. I’ve mainly just been dealing with the rapidly enlarging left breast mass over the last four weeks.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been feeling unusually stressed or overwhelmed lately?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I wouldn’t say I’ve been unusually stressed or overwhelmed—my main concern is really the rapidly enlarging mass in my left breast over the past four weeks.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you experienced any burning or discomfort when you urinate?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t had any burning or discomfort when I urinate. I’ve mainly been focused on the rapidly enlarging mass in my left breast over the past four weeks.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been feeling chills lately?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t had chills or felt feverish—I haven’t noticed anything like that. My main issue is still the rapidly enlarging mass in my left breast over the past four weeks.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed a lump in your breast that feels firm and hasn’t moved?
turns.patient_answer: “Yes—the lump in my left breast feels firm to me, and it hasn’t really moved. It’s been rapidly increasing in size over the past four weeks, and I’ve still had no pain or skin/nipple changes.”

turns.doctor_question: Are you feeling any pain or discomfort on the sides of your abdomen, between your ribs and hips?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any pain or discomfort on the sides of my abdomen between my ribs and hips. My only main concern is the firm lump in my left breast that’s been rapidly getting bigger over the past four weeks.”
